source: segmentation (Blender simulation with background replaced by white)
pixel_axes: x right, y down (image rows); +y = downward on screen

camera.motion: static (rendered fixed camera; background is uniform white so no texture to check, but the plane's x stays at 671 +/- 1 px, so there is no sideways drift)
camera.view: planar, top-down / face-on view of the plane's planform (no visible perspective, constant apparent size)

objects.name: airplane
objects.description: the only object: small yellow/orange propeller-style plane seen from directly above (planform), nose pointing DOWN the image, tail (small horizontal stabiliser) at the top, straight wings across
objects.visible_frames: 0-78 (fully in frame 0-75; nose cut by the bottom edge in 76; only the tail visible in 77-78; gone in 79)
objects.reference_point: ref_x, ref_y = bbox centre of the frame-0 mask (tail tip to nose, wingtip to wingtip), carried to later frames by template matching. Likely origin location; the alternative mask centroid in frame 0 is (671.2, 168.5), 8.5 px lower, and the wing line is at y = 176 in frame 0

size_px_frame0_static_sharp.note: Frame 0 is sharp. Later frames have vertical motion blur, so the mask length grows to 109-114 px; wingspan stays 165-168 px. Use frame 0 (or frames 0-10) for sizes.

objects.motion_summary: Straight vertical drop: moves only +y (down the screen), x constant at 671. Speeds up steadily from rest at frame 0. Per-frame step is about 0.5 px at frame 1, about 13 px at frame 20, about 46 px at frame 75. A quadratic in frame number fits ref_y with RMS 1.1 px (QA only, not a model to use).
objects.orientation: no visible rotation (wingspan constant, nose always down)

static_objects: none: the background is uniform white (segmentation). There is no ground, horizon or markings.

events.event: start of motion / release from rest
events.note: displacement 0->1 is ~0.5 px and grows linearly, so the plane starts at (or very near) rest at frame 0

events.event: nose reaches the bottom image edge
wings out of frame, only tail visible
unrelated mountain/snow image (segmentation artefact, not part of the scene)
